_README: A ledger of claims this project has retracted, superseded, or downgraded to unverified,
and of citations it has ruled unsuitable. It is the machine-readable counterpart to the
correction notes written in prose in PROJECT.md.
It exists because a correction that lands in one file does not propagate to the others.
PROJECT.md recorded on 2026-09-22 that the Davari random-label attribution is unverified
and that the ICLR 2023 venue was dropped pending verification; CLAUDE.md, README.md and
both proposal files continued to assert both. The n = 20 rerun on 2026-09-21 replaced the
2.94x / 1.13x seed-stability figures; csci-proposal-FINAL.md still states them as current
fact and csci-proposal-draft.md states them in its introduction while reporting the
corrected pair later in the same document.
Every entry here names the correction that created it and the file that records that
correction in prose. analysis/consistency_checks.py reads this file and reports any
deliverable that contradicts it. The ledger states what was retracted; it does not decide
what to do about a hit, which remains a matter for the author.
An entry is removed when the underlying claim is verified rather than when it becomes
inconvenient. Removing one is a visible diff, which is the same protection the commit

reason: Dated coursework artifacts, each submitted before later corrections landed.
progress-report-1.md was submitted 2026-09-14, progress-report-2.md 2026-09-29 and
midterm-report.md 2026-10-06. They are historical records of what was believed at the
time and are not retroactively corrected, so the superseded-value check skips them.
Checks that concern citations still apply, because a citation was either verified or it
was not. progress-report-3.md is deliberately NOT frozen: it is the current deliverable
and every check applies to it.
The two proposal drafts and video-script.md were removed from the deliverables list
because the files no longer exist; a check that cannot find its target reports nothing
and quietly stops being a check.

heldout_markers: inputs it did not train on

Unrefereed preprint. Known to be real but unsuitable as authority.

retracted_attributions.name: davari-probe-accuracy-numerals
reason: This entry replaces davari-random-label-arm and davari-venue-iclr-2023, both
retracted on 2026-09-22 and both verified on 2026-11-08. What was verified, and how:
the random-label memorization arm is Section 4.1 of arXiv:2210.16156, which compares
a network trained to generalize on CIFAR10, a network trained to memorize it with
random target labels, and an untrained random network; the linear-probe comparison
across those three is Appendix B.6, Figure 16; and the ICLR 2023 venue is confirmed
from the ICLR 2023 programme page, not from arXiv, whose record for this paper
carries no venue field. Both claims may now be asserted.
What remains retracted is narrower, and is why this entry exists rather than nothing:
the specific probe accuracies of roughly 70% versus 10%. Figure 16 plots them and
does not tabulate them, so the paper states no numeral and no one here has read
values off the plot. Cite the contrast qualitatively or cite the figure; do not state
the numbers.

retracted_attributions.name: founder-identity-beyond-frequency
reason: Control C-4S ran on 2026-10-20 under a rule committed 2026-10-15 and failed both
gates. Founder generation-0 predicted class frequency alone correlates with death
generation at 0.4721 over 10000 within-chain permutations, p = 1e-4, which is a
larger correlation than the 0.3625 transmitted-count effect C-4T rests on. The
committed consequence is explicit: the surviving-alphabet overlap cannot be
attributed to founder identity beyond frequency without a frequency-matched
overlap null, and that null becomes a prerequisite for any further statement about
founder identity rather than an improvement to the statistics.
The 2.12x same-founder overlap ratio is not withdrawn and the n = 20 measurement
stands. What is withdrawn is reading it as evidence of founder identity without
saying what it adds over founder class frequency. Either phrasing of the claim may
be restored once analysis/overlap_stats.py's frequency_matched_null has been run on
logs/seed_stability_n20.json, which needs no new training and is already written.
The patterns here match the two sites where the ratio is asserted as a
founder-identity result and deliberately not the paragraphs that record its
correction history, where stating the number is the point.

retracted_attributions.name: c8-tolerance-data-free-directions
reason: Entered 2026-10-23. The retraction itself was made on 2026-10-20 at commit 3495920 and
until now existed only in that commit message and in the runner's docstring, with no
ledger entry. The founder-identity retraction made the same day got a full entry and this
one did not. That asymmetry is the failure this file's own README describes - a correction
that lands in one file does not propagate to the others - so it is recorded here before a
deliverable repeats it rather than after.
What was retracted. A commit at da82099 reported the Laplace-versus-SGD predicted-class
disagreement as 0.016113 and diagnosed the cause as data-free directions in the posterior.
Both are wrong. The 0.016113 was read at generation 5, where only 6 of 50 classes appear in
the transmitted batch, which is C-4 gate B's failure shape: a statistic read where the
problem has already collapsed. The MAP's out-of-span fraction was then measured at
1.99e-15, so the posterior mean already lives in the data span and data-free directions are
not the cause; projecting SGD onto the span moves the disagreement by +0.0015 while
changing SGD's own predictions on 9.9 percent of points.
What replaced it, measured 2026-10-23 and logged. The fault was two defects in
controls/c8_frozen_body.py, both now fixed: the SGD side minimized AdamW's decoupled decay
rather than the posterior's objective, leaving SGD 3576 nats above the MAP, and the head
carried a bias the no-intercept GLM never fitted. With both fixed the generation-1
disagreement is 0.140625 against a seed-spread interval of [0.136609, 0.190407] at 40 of 50
classes present, inside the tolerance (logs/c8_tolerance.json). The unfixed value at
generation 1 is 0.487549, which reproduces the retraction's own '0.4875 at 1500 steps' to
six digits.
One disagreement is left standing rather than resolved, per CLAUDE.md's rule that two
sources which disagree are reported side by side. The 2026-10-20 correction records the
generation-1 figure as 0.498291; the 2026-10-23 reproduction of the same unfixed quantity
gives 0.487549. Which pool or seed produced the former is not established, so both are
stated and neither is presented as the current value - the current value is 0.140625, which
is a different quantity because the code it measures has been fixed.
The patterns match the retracted figure and the retracted causal claim. The analytic module
is NOT retracted: analysis/laplace_glm.py reproduces its own MAP under LBFGS to 2.40e-06 in
weights and 0.000000 in predictions, so nothing here is a reason to doubt it.

superseded_values.reason: Mean surviving alphabet for C-1's intact arm from three seeds per arm, reported 2026-09-14 against 1.3 for the shuffled arm and described as roughly a factor of nine. The n = 20 rerun (logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json, chain seeds 600 to 619) gives 7.50 with a 95 percent interval of [5.65, 9.25] intact against 1.45 [1.20, 1.70] shuffled, a ratio of 5.17x. Entered 2026-10-23: C-1's own verdict_if_passed in gates/thresholds.json instructs recording the n = 3 figure as superseded the same way 2.94x was, and that instruction had not been carried out, so check 4 was not guarding it. Only 11.3 is listed and not 1.3, because number_pattern('1.3') also matches section references such as section 1.3, the 1.3 hours runtime estimate, and the prior sd 1.3 in the sampler exactness check. Both deliverables that state the superseded pair state it as 11.3 against 1.3, so guarding 11.3 catches any restatement of either number.
Same-founder Jaccard ratio from five chains with ten pairwise comparisons and no interval. The n = 20 rerun (logs/seed_stability_n20.json) gives 2.12x against the empirical null, with a 95% interval.
Cross-founder Jaccard ratio from five chains. The n = 20 rerun gives 0.93x against the empirical null.

Generation-20 agreement with generation 0 at tau = 1.0, B = 4096, measured on the training pool. Control C-6 established that the published pilot agreements are training metrics; the held-out generation-25 value is 0.130.
Generation-20 training-pool agreement at tau = 0.5, B = 4096. Held-out generation-25 value is 0.138; the gap of 0.081 breached the preregistered C-6 threshold.

Generation-20 training-pool agreement under argmax transmission. The held-out generation-25 value is 0.167, a gap of 0.487, and the gap at generation 1 is 0.753. Argmax preserves the founder's memorized lookup table on memorized points, not its function.

evidence: cka_prev is written only by spike_iterated_distill.py and appears only in the six
pilot .jsonl logs, all of which are training-pool runs. controls/c6_probe_pool.py
computes cka_gen0 on the probe pool and never computes a consecutive-generation CKA.
No held-out consecutive-generation CKA value exists anywhere in this repository.
reason: Pairing a consecutive-generation CKA with a held-out agreement figure presents two
measurements from different pools as one observation. The CKA figure that is unaffected
by the pool is cka_gen0 (0.642 training against 0.650 held-out), which is a different
quantity from the one the claim rests on.
Each arm of the seed-stability sweep yields two ratios: observed Jaccard over the
analytic random-subset baseline, which the log prints, and observed Jaccard over the
empirical null, which analysis/seed_stability_stats.py computes and the deliverables
quote. Both are correct and they are measured against different nulls.
CLAUDE.md requires that two sources which disagree be reported side by side and never
quietly resolved into one. Arm A's pair (1.99x analytic, 2.12x empirical) is flagged in
CLAUDE.md and .claude/fence_test.md. Arm C's pair (1.73x, 1.27x) is discussed in
PROJECT.md. Arm B's analytic ratio has never appeared in any deliverable.
